name: Obed-edom
overview: Obed-edom is a male Levite known for his role as a second rank Levite and gatekeeper, specifically assigned to the south gate as noted in 1 Chronicles 15:18 and 26:15. His duties highlight his important service in the temple worship system, reflecting the Levites' sacred responsibility. There are no additional notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Obed-edom means 'servant [worshiper] of Edom,' which is a proper name not given by God, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:18. This name indicates a personal identity connected to worship, consistent with his Levitical role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Obed-edom as a descendant of Levi, confirming his tribal lineage (1 Chronicles 15:18). Several inferred paternal relationships are noted from 1 Chronicles 26:4-5, including Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai, though these appear to represent a genealogical context rather than direct fatherhood.
scriptureSignificance: Obed-edom's significance lies in his trusted position within the Levitical order as a gatekeeper, responsible for the south gate of the temple. This role underscores his contribution to the orderly worship and safeguarding of the sacred space, emphasizing the holiness and reverence required in the service of God. His mention in the chronicler's record affirms the importance of faithful service in the house of the Lord.
